characters.name: Utena Tenjou
characters.description: Action Girl: Her duels take place almostOnce an Episode, and she's extremely athletic. And even outside of the duels, she's tough in both personality and physical ability. She can jump, she can punch, she's a demon on the basketball court, and she can beat trained combat sport specialists with broken bamboo practice swords and brooms. Adaptational Angst Upgrade: In the movie, Utena has not only lost her parents, as in the series, but alsoTouga. He comforted her after her parents died and so losing him was a major blow to her, adding to the sense of loss she already had with her parents. Adaptational Jerkass: Downplayed, but in the movie, Utena is aggressive in her initial interactions with Anthy and it gets to the point whereUtena ends up attacking and pinning Anthy down. Most of this is because of the aboveAdaptational Angst Upgradewith Anthy pressing Utena's buttons in regards to Touga. It is only after the two dance thatUtena becomes entirely cordial with Anthy as she is in the series. Adaptational Sexuality: Utena in the series isimplied to be bisexual, but she isin denial about being attracted to Anthy. In the movie, Utena is clearly and unreservedly bisexual, having no hesitation about romantic interest with Touga or Anthy. Adaptation Dye-Job:The earliest sketches from the manga depict her with hazel eyes (although some illustrations also had them blue.) After the anime came out, the manga mirrors the pink hair and blue eyes found in the televised version.Her uniform is also pink in the early parts of the manga (though she receives a black jacket in volume 3), while in the anime her uniform jacket is black from start.In the first theatrical musical she has black hair with a pink streak. The revival musicals make extensive use of elaborate wigs, allowing Utena to return to pink hair.

characters.name: Anthy Himemiya
characters.description: The Rose Bride of the dueling games, she becomes engaged to whoever can best her current betrothed in a duel. It is said that this person shall gain from her the power to bring the world revolution. She has little autonomy of her own and is unpopular with most students, but she is coveted by the duelists of the Student Council due to her role in their game. Adaptational Consent: Downplayed. While the nature ofher incestuous relationship with Akiocan by definition never be consensual due tothe huge power imbalance between the two, the method by whichAkio rapes herdiffers between mediums.TV series Anthycomplies with Akio's desires due to her devotion to him that he cultivates with emotional manipulation. In the one instance where she does not instantly cave in to his demands, Akio grabs her rather forcefully, exposing how the relationship stems from Akio's hold over her.In the manga, the curse of the Rose Bride makes Anthysubservient to Akio. Her apparent love and loyalty to him are compulsory as long as she serves as the sheath of the Sword of Dios, but after she and Akio successfully plot to transfer the role of Rose Bride to Utena, Anthy is no longer bound to him.In the movie, Anthyisdrugged by Akio, whose dialogue implies that he has done this before to take advantage of her sexually. But when he finds that she isn't unconscious during his molestation, he is the one who panics. However, just as in the anime, Anthy accepts anything he does to her regardless. characters.name: The Student Council in general
characters.description: Absurdly Powerful Student Council: They apparently have enough pull with the powers-that-be at the school that they can get students expelled, and it’s implied they’re responsible for campus security. Even school faculty fears ending up on their bad side. And that's before getting into any of the talk about "revolutionizing the world," which is as absurdly powerful as it comes. Beautifully subverted when it turns out thatnone of them know what "revolutionizing the world" actually means or what the purpose of the dueling game is. Not even Touga knows those answers, even though he is more-or-less a shill for the End of the World that keeps the others invested in the game. The Cavalry Arrives Late: During the Black Rose arc,they're alarmed by the appearance of these new Duelists, who are both targeting the Student Council and want to kill Anthy, who is necessary to revolutionize the world. The very episode they start trying to do anything about it, poring through the school archives for clues about their unknown enemy, Utena defeats Mikage in a duel, leading to him and the threat of the Black Roses being erased from memory. Custom Uniform: Instead of the standard Ohtori Academy uniform, they all wear elaborate military-style uniforms; not even these uniforms are exactly the same, as they're all accented with different colors to distinguish them. Elite Four: The first arc opens with four duelists competing against Utena: Saionji, Juri, Miki, and Touga. These four make up the Student Council, and they are the primary antagonists vying for the power to revolutionize the world... in the beginning at least. Later on in the series, the antagonistic dynamic breaks down as the characters go through their respective development arcs. Friendly Rivalry: They are generally cordial towards Utena and one another, despite their involvement in the winner-take-all dueling game. Juri and especially Miki are good examples of the dynamic, while Touga presents an upstanding outward display

characters.name: Touga Kiryuu
characters.description: Abusive Parents:InAdolescence of Utena, his adoptive father raped him after his birth parents sold him and his sister to the Kiryuu family.According to lead scriptwriter Yoji Enokido, this backstory informs Touga's characterization in the TV series even though it does not feature in the story directly. Adaptation Dye-Job: His manga look features black hair with red forelocks framing his face. In the anime his hair is entirely red, with one forelock a lighter shade of red. After the anime started airing, color manga art gives Touga all red hair, sometimes with a highlighted forelock, sometimes without. His eyes also change from brown to blue. Adaptational Heroism: RetroactiveAll There in the Manualbackstory notwithstanding, TV series Touga is a distinctly dark version of the character who causes significant anguish to the people around him while suffering relatively little in return. Other continuities cast him in a more positive light.In the manga, Touga emotionally manipulates Utena much as he does in the TV series,but unlike the TV series, he is not allied with Akio.He tries his best to save Utenafrom Akio, even telling her that Akio is the End of the World, but he turns his back on Utena after she confesses that she's still attracted to Akio even after he owns up to his foul deeds.InAdolescence of Utenahe is more genuinely heroic compared to the TV series, although his behavior and personality are still open to multiple interpretations. His scenes with Shiori highlight hisFreudian Excuse, and the fact that he fraternizes with Shiori signifies that there is darkness in both of them. However, the most important aspect of Touga in narrative terms ends up being his doomed heroism. characters.name: Juri Arisugawa
characters.description: Action Girl: She leads the fencing club and gives Utena a really hard time in their duels. She is more specifically aLady of Warwho consistently outclasses Utena in sword-fighting ability, yet she never wins. Adaptation Dye-Job: She has blonde hair and brown eyes in Saito's earliest color illustrations, which switches to orange hair and blue eyes in the anime and later color manga illustrations. Adaptational Badass: Played with. In Chapter 11 of the manga, she gives Utenahell, but Utena manages to defeat her head-on.In the TV series she is even more capable. Not only does she still give Utena a hard time, but she also counters the Power of Dios and remains the only duelist in the show that Utena never outfights.The movie circles back to the manga dynamic where Juri is, as usual, a fierce competitor, but Utena beats her fair and square. Adaptational Sexuality:In the TV series, she's a closeted lesbian who is secretly in love with her childhood frenemy Shiori.In the manga, she's heterosexual and in love with Tougabut secretly carries a torch for Ruka and just sees Touga as a stand-in in Ruka's absence; notably, Shiori does not feature in the manga at all.Part of the reason for this seems to be that in the manga, Juri steps into the mean girl role which Nanami occupies in the TV series (including the Nanami'sClingy Jealous Girltendencies regarding Touga). In interviews,Chiho Saitosaid that since the manga was shorter, she wanted to keep the story as focused on Utena as possible, so she decided that Juri's love triangle couldn't be as separate from the main character as it was in the anime. TheAfter the Revolutionmanga epilogue Saito did 20 years later reversed this decision to an extent, showing a now-adult Juri in a relationship with Shiori.InAdolescence of Utena, Juri's attraction to Shiori is alluded to but made less explicit. She also appears to flirt with Miki, but is interrupted before the audience has time to assess her intentions.The movie-manga andLight Novels

characters.name: Kyouichi Saionji
characters.description: Aesop Amnesia: Ironically, Saionji is the first character that repeatedly gets very close to breaking his ownVicious Cyclethroughout the series: Whenever he is spotted in a position where he is no longer a member of the Student Council, he becomes downright affable and pitiable, as with his aspirations thoroughly brought to a halt, hisInferiority Superiority Complexis no longer in effect. However, hewantsto be a part of the Student Council no matter what woes he endures, and while he ultimately gets close to breaking it, but ultimately lacks the capability in the very end,which is why he chooses to support Touga in his goals. Ambiguously Bi: It's hinted that Saionji may just be gay, but the series itself never comes to a decisive conclusion. He's extremely possessive and abusive to Anthy, and talks about her as if she were a doll that can never disobey and stays with him forever. While he does talk about his love for her, he also implies he doesn't view her as a person. On the other hand, he is obsessed with Touga, and one-upping him seems to be his motivation in life. When Saionji and Touga get on better terms late in the TV series, theHomoerotic Subtextbetween them increases precipitously.Saionji even accompanies Touga to the dueling arena as his "bride".That said, it'salsohinted that any genuine attraction Saionji may have felt towards women is overshadowed by his inferiority complex and inability to understand what women are actually feeling. Ax-Crazy: He tries to kill Utena in Chapter 9 of the manga and episode 9 of the TV series. His attack is premeditated in the manga, while the equivalent plotline in the anime is more of a crime of passion. Always Someone Better: No matter what he does, Touga always seems to be one step ahead of him. He is bitter because he believes Touga has surpassed him, and deep down he wants to have his childhood friendship with Touga back. Big Jerk on Campus: He's captain of the kendo club and widely popular among his fellow students f

characters.name: Miki Kaoru
characters.description: Adaptation Dye-Job: An early manga color illustration shows him with brown hair and brown eyes, but in later artwork, Saito colors him to match his anime color scheme with blue hair and blue eyes. Brilliant, but Lazy: Deconstructed. Miki is very accomplished, yet consistently ineffectual due to his wishy-washy nature. He lacks self-confidence, so even when he recognizes the need to take a stand over the unfairness of the world around him, he is easily dissuaded or redirected. Barely Changed Dub Name: Micky in the Latin American dub, which is almost indistinguishable from his original name, and technically breaks theOne-Steve Limitwith Akio (who is named Mike in that dub). Character Tics: He repeatedly times things on a stopwatch he carries — usually he is timing the length of the preceding line of dialogue. Why, and to what end, he does this is aRiddle for the Ages; Miki claims he does it as a "kind of fortune-telling", but he gives this answer in a somewhat-joking and evasive manner. The musical adaptationBud of the White Rosehas Miki claim that he uses the stopwatch to time exactly how long he spends hating the Student Council. (The exact percentage of time was apparently ad-libbed on every night of the show's run.) Compulsory School Age: He is studying university coursework, but is in his first year of middle school and thus an underclassman to almost every other character. Since he is a very mannerly boy, he takessenpai/kouhairelationships seriously despite operating on a higher intellectual level than most of his seniors.

characters.name: Nanami Kiryuu
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: She is part of the wealthy Kiryuu family and has built-in social clout as the younger sibling of the Student Council president. She goes to great lengths to assert her superiority over her fellow students, and surrounds herself with aGirl Possewho does the dirty work of harassing the targets of her wrath so she can maintain aClass Princessfaçade. She becomes a deconstruction of the trope as the story advances; Nanami positioning her social life on being the leader of aGirl Possemeans that she doesn't actually trust any of her friends on an emotional level. She also is unable to affect anything she actually cares about because her older brother has even more social power than her. Animals Hate Her: Various animals antagonize her, including elephants on surfboards and akangaroo wearing boxing gloves. Her bizarre misfortunes go largely unexplained, but are hinted to be karmic punishment forkilling Touga's kitten when she was younger,orAnthy getting magical payback on her for bullying her.Or both. Animal Motifs:In "Cowbell of Happiness", she stubbornly wears a cowbell until she turns into a cow herself. While this is mostly a played-for-laughsKarmic Transformation, Nanami's cow nightmare where Touga ships her to market and then eats Nanami-steak highlights a darker aspect of her character — her brother is metaphorically rearing her for slaughter by manipulating her insecurities so she will participate in the dueling game.To go even further, the climax of Nanami's character arc suggests that Touga is trying to groom her into his own personal Rose Bride, a fate which she narrowly avoids.In the movie, she justisa cow. There's no context. In "Cowbell of Happiness", she stubbornly wears a cowbell until she turns into a cow herself. characters.name: Souji Mikage
characters.description: Ambiguously Bi: With a particular focus on the "ambiguous" aspect. His behavior as Nemuro suggests he fancied Tokiko and is still hung up on her in the present...but only as she was when he knew her, since he does not recognize the adult she has become.His interactions with Mamiya as Nemuro straddle the line betweenShip TeaseandPlatonic Writing, Romantic Reading. Meanwhile, in the present as Mikage his romantic and/or sexual overtures toward Mamiya are comparatively blatant, like the scene where Mikage kisses Mamiya's hand when he pricks his finger on a rose, and Mamiya does not push back on Mikage's insinuations that he injured himself deliberately. Ambiguous Situation: Most of his characterization derives from subtext and there is little about him that can be said for certain.His presentation suggests that he is an authority figure, yet dialogue states he is a high school senior. He is never shown doing any normal student activities.In his past as Professor Nemuro, he looks even more like an authority figure given the clear contrast between him and students he works with, but he engages in more naïve behaviors than he does in the present.The information given about his identity and history are contradictory, and the nature of his existence itself is uncertain.Viewers often conclude Mikage wasDead All Along, but the narrative carefully avoids affirming or denying this.It's not clear what happens to him when his story draws to a close.Most of the characters forget that he was ever there, and even the rumors about the 100 boys buried alive is contradicted in the end, replaced with hearsay that no one died in the fire that destroyed the research building after all. When Akio takes Mikage's call after he loses his duel, Akio tells him he has "graduated", without any details on what this means.He even demonstratesambidexterity. His presentation suggests that he is an authority figure, yet dialogue states he is a high school senior. He is never shown doing any normal stu

characters.name: The Duelists in general
characters.description: Members of the Ohtori Academy student body who were brainwashed by Mikage’s seminar to fight Utena, in the name of killing the Rose Bride. Brainwashed and Crazy: To an extent. The Mikage Seminar interviews areMore than Mind Control; by encouraging the interviewees to admit their deepest, darkest fears, Mikage is able to redirect their feelings of alienation toward obtaining the power to revolutionize the world. In order to get that, they must first defeat Utena, and the relationship they had with Utena before attending the seminar no longer seems to matter to them once they accept Mikage's black rose and signet ring. But Mikage's manipulation only works if the subject's doubts and fears are bound up in destructive impulses,as seen in the rejection of Tatsuya—he expresses his faith in love, and Mikage tells him that the seminar is no place for him. Deconstructed Character Archetype: Each of them deconstructSatellite Character, each in their own way; theirCynicism Catalystis invariably the resentment they feel over being merely a supporting characterin someone else's life. Disproportionate Retribution: They are usually motivated by a small or perceived slight which is depicted as emblematic of their whatever their dilemma happens to be. For example,Kozue discovers that her provocative behavior is not as effective at drawing Miki's attention as it was before he started crushing on Anthy, and in the next scene Kozue attends the Mikage Seminar and becomes a Black Rose duelist.Inevitably, fighting Utena in order to kill Anthy is an extreme overreaction which often has no connection to their underlying problem. Knights of Cerberus: Their arrival increases the stakes of the duels: while the Student Council members wanted to take Anthy for themselves, the Black Rose duelists want to kill her.

characters.name: Wakaba Shinohara
characters.description: The Ace: After sheltering Saionji in her room and gaining his attention (so she believes), Wakaba becomes one of these, with a montage showing her excelling in all her academic and athletic classes. It's implied that she was always this talented, but having Saionji act as aMagic Feathercaused her confidence to rise. All Girls Want Bad Boys: In her mind's eye, Saionji is accomplished, sporty, and widely-admired — she seems to completely gloss over the undesirable aspects of his personality. They connect when Saionji is vulnerable enough to need her help, and he shows more decency toward her than to anyone in the series up to that point. As much as living a quiet life with Wakaba gives Saionji room to be a nicer person, his mind is not really on her. It's on himself and getting back to his position of power in the school. Ambiguously Bi: Wakaba calls Utena her "boyfriend" and her "true love", and is super clingy towards her in a way that's mostlyPlayed for Laughs, but still has some sincerity. Her attractions to boys, on the other hand, tend to be played for drama and are consequential to the plot. She kicks off the main plot when Saionji mocks the love letter she sent him. Changing of the Guard: The end of the series hints thatWakaba is stepping into a role similar to the one Utena had now that she's gone. She has a new best friend who dotes on her the way Wakaba doted on Utena, and her friendship with Tatsuya seems to be in a better place. Cool Car: In the movieshe is one of the characters who turn into a car. She downplays the trope by being a less flashy car than the other characters — she is a green Jeep. What she lacks in flair she makes up for in heroics, because her reveal as a car is aBig Damn Heroesmoment. Her car formalso sports severalbeginner driver markers; the symbol for this is colloquially called the "wakaba mark" in Japan.

characters.name: Kozue Kaoru
characters.description: Adaptation Personality Change: The manga version of Kozue is very different from the anime version. In the manga she is bratty and overprotective of Miki, but strictly aSatellite Character. In the anime she is one of several Satellite Character deconstructions found among the Black Rose duelists. Like in the manga, her relationship with her brother is very important to her and something she intends to safeguard, but her approach to protecting it often seems counter-intuitive until she gets herDay in the Limelight. And sometimes even then. Ambiguously Bi: Kozue is frequently seen flirting with boys and men, but occasionally fools around with girls as well.In episode 26, she comes on to Anthy during Miki's duel, and appears to make out with her just out of view of the "camera".Kozue and theArc VillainChigusa are seen on dates together multiple times in the visual novel, and when questioned about their association, Kozue insists that she can date anyone she pleases, including girls. In episode 26, she comes on to Anthy during Miki's duel, and appears to make out with her just out of view of the "camera". Kozue and theArc VillainChigusa are seen on dates together multiple times in the visual novel, and when questioned about their association, Kozue insists that she can date anyone she pleases, including girls. Ascended Extra: The manga version of Kozue is aClingy Jealous Girltowards Miki who isput in dangerin order tomotivate Miki to duel, and she has no role in the story after being rescued. The TV series expands her personality to the point that her motivations are challenging to parse and gives her aDay in the Limelight.

characters.name: Shiori Takatsuki
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: InAfter the Revolution, Shiori and Juri's relative social positions are reversed, with Shiori characterized as a classy, beautiful princess whom Juri aspired to be a prince to in her youth. The story is primarily set in their adult years, in which Juri is a professional fencer and fashion model, with Shiori her close friend and manager. It is the most positive relationship shown between them in any continuity. Adaptational Sexuality: In the TV series, Shiori dates boys, but her toxic obsession with Juri encourages an interpretation (cofirmed byWord of God) that Shiori actually loves Juri back but is in deep denial about it. InAdolescence of Utena, Shiori is genuinely attracted to Touga (or at least her perception of him), and shows no sign of reciprocating Juri's feelings. Adaptational Villainy: In the TV series Shiori has no grand motives and nothing against anyone but Juri, but she is indifferent to the effect her actions have on anyone who gets caught up in her attempts to hurt Juri.Adolescence of Utenaupgrades her into a broader, more destructive force whose envy grows to include not just Juri, but Utena and Anthy. She blames Juri forrobbing her of her prince, Touga. Due to this, she manipulates Juri's affections to force Juri to be her prince insteadand uses this to manipulate her into a duel with Utena. Adapted Out: Shiori does not appear in the base manga or the movie adaptation manga; the manga creator Chiho Saito chose to omit her to keep the focus on the protagonists. The only part of manga where Shiori appears isAfter the Revolution. Always Someone Better: Shiori's poor self-opinion caused her to poison her relationship with Juri, believing that someone as beautiful and talented as Juri must have ulterior motives for befriending someone as unremarkable as her. Shiori made it her goal to level the playing field between them by dragging Juri down, but she finds no satisfaction in it since the competition only exists in her mind. Juri

characters.name: Kanae Ohtori
characters.description: Adapted Out: Kanae does not appear in the initial run of the manga, where no mention is ever made of Akio having a fiancée. However, she does figure in a few scenes in the movie manga,and she blames Anthy for Akio's death. Arranged Marriage: Her father arranged a match between her and Akio because, as she describes it, her father was impressed with Akio. She shows nothing but positivity towards her fiancée at first. Cute and Psycho: She seems mature and well-adjusted, but is quickly revealed to be emotionally brittle.She is so uncomfortable with her inability to get along with Anthy that Mikage and Mamiya are able to turn her to violence. It doesn't help that her initiation as a Black Rose duelist is particularly harrowing — Mamiya stabs her black rose into her chest. Dark Action Girl:The very first one introduced in the Black Rose arc. Her fight with Utena is short, given that she's a sort of facsimile duelist with a weak and distorted motivation, but her unexpected appearance in the duel arena does cause Utena a bit of stress. Dark Mistress: Played with.Kanae's position suggests that she is Akio's love interest, but he cares about her as much as he cares about anyone else... which is to say, not at all. Kanae is as much in the dark about Akio's true nature as her father seemingly was, and approaches her impending marriage to him forthrightly. She is nothing more than a pawn, and Akio seems to have managed her family well enough that he doesn't even need to marry her to control them by the third arc of the series. It's even implied that he poisons her at that point, just to demonstrate how unimportant she is to his plans.

characters.name: Keiko Sonoda
characters.description: Backstabbing the Alpha Bitch: HerDay in the Limelightreveals thatshe is deeply resentful of Nanami, whom she views as the sole barrier that keeps her from pursuing her dreams. Keiko becomes an enthusiastic pawn in Touga's scheme to undermine Nanami when Touga offers her the one thing she always wanted — his attention. Having Touga in her corner makes her bold enough to give Nanami a taste of her own medicine,but Keiko is still aThin-Skinned Bullyat heart. As soon as she she gets push-back, she retreats into subservience again. Beta Bitch: She is a classic example. As Nanami's enforcer she coordinates and executes Nanami's wishes, managing the logistics of her schemes and coordinating the other members of theGirl Posseto enact them. It's clear that Keiko is the one who leads Aiko and Yuuko, and of the girl posse members, she is the one who delivers the most lines and gets the most focus. Nanami treats her like a servant and punishes her harshly the moment she steps out of line. Boss Banter: It is commonfor the Black Rose Dueliststorant about their grievances, but Keiko is the most talkative. Granted,all the Black Rose Duelists only borrow their competency from the soul swords they take from the student council members, but Keiko seems disinterested in fighting Utenaand just rambles about her love for Touga and her desire to remove Nanami from the picture —permanently. Cinderella Plot: Subverted. At first, Keiko's arc seems to follow this trope straight to the point of parody with Nanami playing the role of the "evil stepmother". But even though Nanami mistreats Keiko, she is not a sympatheticperfect victim. Her prince, Touga, is not the ideal figure she imagines him to be either, but she would rather have him than have her dignity.And her fairy tale goes well and truly off the rails when her "ball" turns out to be a sword fight with a girl who doesn't really have anything to do with her problems.There is noHappily Ever Afterwith her prince —while they do get together

characters.name: Mitsuru Tsuwabuki
characters.description: Adorably Precocious Child: Deconstructed. He is hard-working and responsible, fulfills Nanami's wishes and takes care of her business without her even having to ask, and he takes the desire to be treated like an adult to extremes. However, his confused concept of adulthood leads him tobecome a Black Rose duelist, and his innocence sometimes blinds him to the consequences of his actions. Ambiguous Innocence: Prior to his full introduction, he stalks Nanami, making her afraid for her life. While he has no real desire to harm her, he places her in a series of deadly situationsso he can rescue herand get her to admire and rely on him, apparently not realizing that this isvery bad. Ambiguous Situation: He doesn't seem to know what he wants from his relationship with Nanami. Initially he accepts Nanami's proposition to become her boyfriend, but she treats him like a servant and he accepts this. He reveals to Utena his motivation is to become Nanami's big brother, even though this is a categorically impossible goal. Given Nanami's attraction to Touga, it's unclear whether Tsuwabuki wants to be that big brother because he thinks that's the only way to get Nanami's romantic attention or whether he really wants a familial bond with her. Once the initial misunderstandings between Tsuwabuki and Nanami are cleared up and they stop "dating", he carries on as her personal servant, though not without some growing pains. He longs for Nanami to treat him the way she treats her actual big brother Touga, but the insurmountable age gap between them makes him so frustrated that he falls prey to the Black Rose Society. He does not fully distinguish between romantic intimacy and familial closeness, as seen when he and Nanami break up and he tells her, "if I can't become your big brother, I'll become your little brother". Badass Adorable: He is a charmingly precocious grade school boy who should never be underestimated. He gets into a fight withthreeboys who are Nanami's age, and single-han

characters.name: Tatsuya Kazami
characters.description: Cannot Spit It Out: Tatsuya struggles to find the courage to express his feelings for Wakaba, and when he works up the nerve make his love confession, his phrasing is still too indirect. Their ambiguous conversation about "being true to your feelings"makes it look like they're going to end up together, but thenWakaba wishes him luck finding his special someone, thanking him for his advice before leaving to see hertrueprince, Saionji. Deconstructed Character Archetype: Of aFlat Character. In both past and present, Tatsuya seems entirely unbothered and passive, only showing emotional distress when Wakaba deviates from hisChildhood Friend Romancescript. He compares unfavorably even to the similarly "basic" Aiko as he lacks any comedic quirks or external struggles. This paints Tatsuya as a cringeworthy and fundamentally shallow person who really is as unremarkable as he seems. Demoted to Extra: Tatsuya appears in a few classroom scenes inAdolescence of Utenain a non-speaking role. Dogged Nice Guy: He engages in a downplayed version of persistent support with Wakaba.Despite the crushing disappointment of his failed love confession, he evidently renews his friendship with Wakaba since he is shown hanging out and bantering with her in a handful of scenes later on. The series leaves the door open for aRelationship Upgradebetween them at some point in the future. Embarrassing Nickname: He seems put-out by Wakaba calling him "onion prince", and assumes that she's making fun of him.

characters.name: Tokiko Chida
characters.description: Ambiguous Innocence: Her behavior in episode 22 initially comes off as a woman desperately trying to save her younger brother, but closer inspection reveals she commits several microaggressions against Professor Nemuro to rile him up while deliberately ensuring he would see firsthand Mamiya's state to goad him into continuing his research. Hersleeping with Akiomakes her even shadier. Mamiya's mention of Tokiko's desire to preserve flowers is not an indication of a healthy mindset, as it shows a desire to keep prolonging an unhealthy situation for her own comfort.Episode 23 would later imply that we’re only seeing the Tokiko of Mikage’s altered memories and that, much like he has been remembering a fake Mamiya based on memories he created, the Tokiko here was changed to fit the narrative Mikage built for himself (and that Akio and Anthy helped enforce on him). That the ostensibly “real” Tokiko is shown slapping Nemuro after he set the fire gives the idea she only ever wanted to help her brother. Big Sister Instinct: She takes an interest in Professor Nemuro based on the understanding that his research will "grasp eternity", because her little brother Mamiya has a terminal illness and she refuses to give up hope of saving him. There is no guarantee that the research will help Mamiya even if it succeeds, but she inspires Nemuro to redouble his efforts on the project nonetheless.Depending on the viewer's interpretation of her actions, she appears to switch allegiance to Akio later on. Or, alternatively, she may have been on Akio's side from the start (she is an agent of the school board, after all,) and may have been stringing Nemuro along. On the other hand, she might have been yet another victim of Akio's manipulations due to Akio and Anthy using her as a convenient scapegoat for Mikage to obsess over. characters.name: Dios
characters.description: Adaptation Dye-Job: The base manga depicts him with dark hair, while in the TV series and movie, his hair is pale purple. Ambiguously Brown: He has a dark skin tone and wears a bindi, similar to Anthy and Akio. Hislight-colored hair and dark skinenhances his otherworldliness and signifies his importance both within the setting and to the narrative. Chronic Hero Syndrome: He feels compelled to save every damsel in distress.This is taken to such an extreme extent that he physically exhausts himself almost to the point of death. After Anthy intervenes on his behalf and becomes a scapegoat for him, he no longer exhibits a need to save anyone. Deconstructed Character Archetype: In the anime, he is one to theIdeal HeroKnight in Shining Armor. Ostensibly, he was a selfless savior and defender of women. Unfortunately, he could not keep up with the demand and pushed himself to the point of collapse. His legacy is a patriarchal system thatelevates a handful of menandsmothers everyone else, keeping peopledependent. His personal life was also nonexistent, leaving his little sister neglected. And seeing as dragons and witches haven't destroyed the world during his centuries-long absence,it's hard to say how much good he even did.Also deconstructs theViolence Really Is the Answermentality that much of fiction defaults to. Dios "saved" many young women from danger, but said danger remains conveniently undefined. What IS clear is that most of the violent characters in the present have very real flaws and insecurities, experiencingCharacter Developmentonly by discarding violence as a tool. Meanwhile, the more Utena herself embraces dueling, the easier she becomes to manipulate; her few genuine successes with Anthy come from come from empathy, not through rescuing her. EvenAkio's defeat is asnonviolent as it is devastating. As cool and flashy as the God-Prince seems, Dios never actually solved a single problem. characters.description: Adapted Out: Downplayed; inAdolescence of Utena, E-ko and F-ko replace A-ko and B-ko, but they are similar in terms of appearance and narrative purpose, and have the same voice actors. Canon Immigrant: C-ko is the only one of the Shadow Girls to be transplanted into the movie, with A-ko and B-ko being replaced by E-ko and F-ko. Catchphrase:A-ko and B-ko routinely incorporate the phrase "Kashira, kashira, gozonji kashira?" characters.name: Chu-Chu
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He wears a red necktie and an earring in one ear, but nothing else.He ditches the tie at the end when he and Anthy cut ties with her brother and leave Ohtori Academy. Animals Not to Scale: He's a monkey, but he's even smaller than the smallest species of monkeys. This frequently leads viewers to mistake him for a mouse. Bare-Bottomed Monkey: In the animated adaptations his posterior is the same color as his face, suggesting that he has no fur there. The manga does not share this design element. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Chu-Chu's are made up of a series of parallel lines — usually about four, but sometimes drawn much denser. They are particularly pronounced in the anime. Blush Sticker: He has reddish patches on his cheeks as a standard part of his character design. In the manga, his cheeks are entirely red.

characters.name: Yuuko Oose and Aiko Wakiya
characters.description: Backstabbing the Alpha Bitch: Aiko and Yuuko fall in line behind Keikowhen Nanami's social dominance wanes during the Akio arc. The three of them bemoan all the time they "wasted" kissing Nanami's ass, but the rebellion is short-lived — Nanami gives them an epic beatdown back into her servitude before her second duel. Bit Character: They appear fairly frequently, but their role is limited to serving asSocial Circle Fillerfor Nanami and Keiko; they only exist to pine after Touga and kiss up to theirAlpha Bitch. Fair Weather Friends: In ''Troublesome Insects", Nanami blacklists Keiko, and Aiko and Yuuko support Nanami by giving Keiko theSilent Treatment— acting as if she isn't there before wondering aloud if they heard someone talking. By the end of the episode Keiko makes up with Nanami and they're all back together again as a posse and professing their loyalty to one another. False Friend: They only hang around Nanami in order to lust after Touga without worrying about Nanami making them miserable, while framing it asUndying Loyaltyto Nanami in order to keep one another from pursuit of Touga. Girl Posse: They are members of Nanami's three-girl clique, along with Keiko. They mostly just stand in the background and look haughty.

characters.name: Yamada, Tanaka, and Suzuki
characters.description: Continuity Cameo: They have a blink-and-you'll-miss-it cameo inAdolescence of Utenaduring the car chase. The Dividual: They only appear as a group, and are for all intents and purposes a single character. Funny Background Event: Their main contribution to the series is doing weird, silly things in the background and getting snubbed by more consequential characters. Hopeless Suitor: They have crushes on Nanami but she can't be bothered to ever remember them. In the last episode they try giving love letters to Keiko, Aiko, and Yuuko.They get shot down again. They get shot down no matter what they're asking for. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: They are indistinguishable except for their hairstyles. They have different surnames (and indeed,Only One Name) so they probably aren't relatives; they're just three of the same guy as a gag.

characters.name: Mari Hozumi
characters.description: Jerk with a Heart of Gold: She is abrasive and consistently critical of Mitsuru's behavior, but it's definitely coming from a place of concern for him. Older and Wiser: Subverted. She pulls the upperclassman card on Mitsuru even though she is only one year ahead of him. However, she does have a point that Mitsuru is going about this "adult experience" situation incorrectly by trying to rush things. One-Shot Character: She only appears in one episode, where she provides a counterpoint to Tsuwabuki's misguided ambition. Only Sane Man: Mari is one of the more grounded characters in the show, and she's always trying to get Mitsuru to stop being Nanami's lackey. Satellite Character: To Mitsuru, hence why she never appears again.

characters.name: Ruka Tsuchiya
characters.description: All for Nothing:He attempts to convince Juri that she would be unstoppable if she didn't let petty people like Shiori hold her back, but once his plans run their course, Shiori and Juri still have strong attachments to one another. The ordeal he put them through even appears to have made their relationship marginally less toxic. Alternatively, if his goal was to free Juri from the misery that her toxic relationship with Shiori brought her even if it meant having to make her hate him to do so, he only succeeded in hurting her even more. Always Someone Better: He is Juri's superior rival—he's not only a better fencer than her, he also starts dating Shiori, the girl Juri loves.And all this while being deathly ill, implying that he would be even better if not for that.Juri shows no sign that she ever thinks she can best him,but she does eventually refuse to play his game, which is a different sort of victory. Back for the Dead: He attended Ohtori Academy in the past but has been absent due to a long illness.He's secretly terminally ill when he returns to the school. Borrowed Catch Phrase: He co-opts part of the Akio Car introduction that is otherwise recited by Touga, and lampshades the borrowing by inviting Touga to deliver the final line. It foreshadows thathe's manipulating Shiori and Juri. Broken Ace: He's a supreme fencer and beloved by most who know him. But he also hasnot much time to liveand just as many emotional issues as the rest of the cast, attempting to 'free' Juri from her bonds to Shiori by any means necessary.

characters.name: Mrs. Ohtori
characters.description: Abusive Parents: She seems like she has her daughter Kanae's interests in mind at first, but this impression only lasts untilshe and Akio are alone together—at which point she reveals herself to be selfish and only interested in the pursuit of her own pleasure. She is having an affair with Akio, her daughter's fiancée, behind her back.Supplemental materialsstate that she is Akio's co-conspirator in poisoning her husband, the real Chairman Ohtori and Kanae's father. Evil Matriarch: She is catastrophically selfish,cavorting with Akioand caring very little about her ill husband's health or Kanae's well-being. She tries to manipulate Akio by reminding him that his position at the Academy depends on her family, buthe completely turns the conversation around with subtle references to her husband's ill health—not to mention the fact that he has hercompletely wrapped around his finger. The Faceless: As with most parents in this series, she is consistently framed so that the viewer only sees her face from oblique angles, and her eyes are never on screen. Fairy Tale Motifs: Her role can best be considered a cross between the Evil Queen and theWicked Stepmotherdespite being Kanae's biological mother. She is an older, vain woman who doesn't care how much she hurts her daughter, andis actively poisoning her husbandso she can live out a fantasy where she's young and beautiful and adored by a prince. Mrs. Ohtori sharing the same cyan color as Chigusa Sanjouin is an indication of her fulfilling the Evil Queen role, as it's frequently used to represent the harm of "forced femininity" since we later see the color used for the earrings Utena receives from Akio. It's All About Me: While she seems like aproper ladyin mixed company, in private she behaves as if her husband's illness is a nuisance to her.In reality, she seems to consider her husband'scontinued existenceto be a nuisance, given that is party to poisoning him. The only thing she wants is to continue her affair with Akio,and

characters.name: Chigusa Sanjouin
characters.description: Arc Villain: She is the primary antagonist of theVisual Novel, and the good endings are achieved by defeating her. Dark Action Girl: An antagonistic female fencer who opposes Utena. She is powerful enough physically to easily overpower the protagonist, and even knocks out the duelists in many routes. Utena cannot defeat her on her own, and requires the protagonist's help to exploit herAchilles' Heel. Dead All Along:Chigusa explicitly states that she died in the fire at the fencing hall 15 years prior and was brought back from the dead by a "certain someone", who is implied to be Akio. Disproportionate Retribution:Chigusa was heartbroken and angry after she received an invitation to Masaomi and Koto's wedding, and she burned the fencing hall down with herself inside it. Death has done nothing to dull her desire for vengeance, and she seeks the power to revolutionize the world so she can go back in time and keep Masaomi and Koto from getting together so the protagonist will beerased from existence. Even the Girls Want Her: She gets her share of squealing from fangirls when she's in class, and she and Kozue are shown out on dates together multiple times.
